claim: The sea anemone hair cell has an apical cilium surrounded by a circle of stereovilli.
source: We first examined the structure of hair cells in the oral tentacles of the sea anemone N. vectensis at the primary polyp stage by light and electron microscopy. We used phalloidin to label F-actin enriched in stereovilli of hair cells, and the lipophilic dye DiI to label the plasma membrane of hair cells. Hair cells are an epithelial cell type whose cell body is pear-shaped and occurs exclusively in the superficial stratum of pseudostratified ectoderm in oral tentacles (Figure 1). The hair cell has an apical cilium surrounded by eight large-diameter stereovilli that extend actin filament-containing rootlets into the cytoplasm (Figure 1B–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1

claim: The sea anemone hair cell has eight large-diameter stereovilli.
source: The hair cell has an apical cilium surrounded by eight large-diameter stereovilli that extend actin filament-containing rootlets into the cytoplasm (Figure 1B–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1

claim: Stereovilli of sea anemone hair cells extend actin filament-containing rootlets into the cytoplasm.
source: The hair cell has an apical cilium surrounded by eight large-diameter stereovilli that extend actin filament-containing rootlets into the cytoplasm (Figure 1B–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1

claim: In primary polyps, the apical cilium of hair cells is 10–15 µm long.
source: In primary polyps, the apical cilium is 10–15 µm long; stereovilli are 3–5 µm long and 200–400 nm in diameter; stereovillar rootlets are 2–3 µm long.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on measurements from microscopy data

claim: In primary polyps, stereovilli of hair cells are 3–5 µm long and 200–400 nm in diameter.
source: In primary polyps, the apical cilium is 10–15 µm long; stereovilli are 3–5 µm long and 200–400 nm in diameter; stereovillar rootlets are 2–3 µm long.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on measurements from microscopy data

claim: In primary polyps, stereovillar rootlets of hair cells are 2–3 µm long.
source: In primary polyps, the apical cilium is 10–15 µm long; stereovilli are 3–5 µm long and 200–400 nm in diameter; stereovillar rootlets are 2–3 µm long.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on measurements from microscopy data

claim: Electron-lucent vesicles ranging from 50 to 100 nm in diameter are abundant in the cytoplasm of a hair cell.
source: Electron-lucent vesicles ranging from 50 to 100 nm in diameter are abundant in the cytoplasm of a hair cell (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1I

claim: Stereovilli of a hair cell are encircled by smaller-diameter microvilli contributed by adjacent support cells.
source: Stereovilli of a hair cell are encircled by smaller-diameter microvilli (80–150 nm) contributed by adjacent support cells that are enriched in electron-dense vacuoles in the apical cytoplasm (Figure 1E–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1

claim: Support cells are enriched in electron-dense vacuoles in the apical cytoplasm.
source: Stereovilli of a hair cell are encircled by smaller-diameter microvilli (80–150 nm) contributed by adjacent support cells that are enriched in electron-dense vacuoles in the apical cytoplasm (Figure 1E–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 1

claim: The ciliary cone of tentacular nematocytes in N. vectensis is less pronounced than that of hair cells.
source: A subset of cnidocytes – nematocytes but not anthozoan-specific spirocytes – forms a morphologically similar apical mechanosensory apparatus known as the ciliary cone (Fautin and Mariscal, 1991); however, the ciliary cone of tentacular nematocytes in N. vectensis is less pronounced than that of hair cells, and consists of a single cilium surrounded by short microvilli (2–2.5 µm long) that lack actin rootlets (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: The ciliary cone of tentacular nematocytes consists of a single cilium surrounded by short microvilli (2–2.5 µm long) that lack actin rootlets.
source: A subset of cnidocytes – nematocytes but not anthozoan-specific spirocytes – forms a morphologically similar apical mechanosensory apparatus known as the ciliary cone (Fautin and Mariscal, 1991); however, the ciliary cone of tentacular nematocytes in N. vectensis is less pronounced than that of hair cells, and consists of a single cilium surrounded by short microvilli (2–2.5 µm long) that lack actin rootlets (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3

claim: A hair cell extends thin neuronal processes basally that likely form synapses with the tentacular nerve net and/or longitudinal muscle fibers.
source: Basally, a hair cell extends thin neuronal processes that likely form synapses with the tentacular nerve net and/or longitudinal muscle fibers located at the base of the ectodermal epithelium alongside mesoglea (Figure 1C, E and G).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1; the synapse formation is inferred

claim: Stereovilli characteristic of hair cells never occur in the circumoral ectoderm during planula development.
source: We next sought to determine the timing of hair cell development by using phalloidin to label stereovilli – the morphological hallmark of hair cells in N. vectensis. We never found stereovilli in the circumoral ectoderm during planula development (Figure 1—figure supplement 4A,B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: Pronounced stereovilli become evident in the circumoral ectoderm at the tentacle-bud stage.
source: However, pronounced stereovilli became evident in the circumoral ectoderm at the tentacle-bud stage (Figure 1—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: The hair cell is a postembryonic cell type that does not initiate development until metamorphosis in N. vectensis.
source: These observations suggest that the hair cell is a postembryonic cell type that does not initiate development until metamorphosis in N. vectensis.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation that stereovilli appear only at the tentacle-bud stage

claim: The N. vectensis genome contains a single gene that encodes the class IV POU homeodomain transcription factor.
source: The N. vectensis genome contains a single gene that encodes the class IV POU homeodomain transcription factor (Nv160868; Tournière et al., 2020; Nakanishi et al., 2010; Gold et al., 2014)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: pou-iv mRNA is strongly expressed in circumoral ectoderm during metamorphosis in N. vectensis.
source: It has been previously shown that pou-iv mRNA is strongly expressed in circumoral ectoderm during metamorphosis in N. vectensis (Tournière et al., 2020), consistent with a role in tentacular morphogenesis.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: pou-iv is expressed in cnidocytes throughout the body including those in the tentacles.
source: Although gene expression analysis using a transgenic reporter line has indicated that pou-iv is expressed in cnidocytes throughout the body including those in the tentacles (Tournière et al., 2020), whether pou-iv is expressed in mechanosensory hair cells is not known.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: The pattern of anti-POU-IV immunoreactivity parallels that of pou-iv mRNA expression.
source: In addition, immunostaining and in situ hybridization experiments showed that the pattern of anti-POU-IV immunoreactivity paralleled that of pou-iv mRNA expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), further supporting the specificity of the antibody.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: POU-IV protein localizes to nuclei of differentiating and differentiated hair cells in the ectoderm of developing tentacles.
source: We therefore used immunostaining with the anti-POU-IV to analyze the expression pattern of POU-IV in developing oral tentacles of N. vectensis at metamorphosis. We found that POU-IV protein localized to nuclei of differentiating and differentiated hair cells, but not to those of support cells, in the ectoderm of developing tentacles (Figure 2A–L).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2

claim: POU-IV protein does not localize to nuclei of support cells in the ectoderm of developing tentacles.
source: We found that POU-IV protein localized to nuclei of differentiating and differentiated hair cells, but not to those of support cells, in the ectoderm of developing tentacles (Figure 2A–L).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 2

claim: Nuclear labeling by the anti-POU-IV was abolished when the antibody was preadsorbed with the POU-IV antigen prior to immunostaining.
source: Nuclear labeling by the anti-POU-IV was abolished when the antibody was preadsorbed with the POU-IV antigen prior to immunostaining (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), evidencing that the antibody reacts with nuclear POU-IV.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3, validating antibody specificity

claim: None of the POU-IV-expressing epithelial cells in the developing tentacles incorporated EdU.
source: As observed for pou-iv transcript-expressing cells during embryogenesis (Tournière et al., 2020), we found that none of the POU-IV-expressing epithelial cells in the developing tentacles examined (n > 220 cells across three tentacle-bud-stage animals and eight primary polyps) incorporated EdU (e.g. Figure 2M–P), indicative of their postmitotic cell-cycle status.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by EdU labeling data shown in Figure 2

claim: POU-IV-expressing cells in the developing tentacles are postmitotic.
source: As observed for pou-iv transcript-expressing cells during embryogenesis (Tournière et al., 2020), we found that none of the POU-IV-expressing epithelial cells in the developing tentacles examined (n > 220 cells across three tentacle-bud-stage animals and eight primary polyps) incorporated EdU (e.g. Figure 2M–P), indicative of their postmitotic cell-cycle status.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the EdU labeling data

claim: Large deletions at the pou-iv locus were readily confirmed by genotyping PCR using genomic DNA extracted from single CRISPR-injected embryos.
source: Multiple sgRNAs were designed to cleave flanking sites of the coding region of the pou-iv locus (Figure 3A; Figure 3—figure supplement 1). Large deletions were readily confirmed by genotyping PCR using genomic DNA extracted from single CRISPR-injected embryos (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by genotyping data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The pou-iv- allele has a 705 bp deletion that removes a sequence encoding most of the POU domain and all of the homeodomain.
source: One of the mutant alleles, which will be here referred to as pou-iv-, had a 705 bp deletion that removed a sequence encoding most of the POU domain (i.e. all but the first four N-terminal residues) and all of the homeodomain at the pou-iv locus (Figure 3B; Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by sequencing data shown in Figure 3

claim: Western blotting confirmed that pou-iv -/- polyps express mutant POU-IV lacking DNA-binding domains but not wildtype POU-IV.
source: Western blotting with the anti-POU-IV has confirmed that pou-iv -/- polyps express mutant POU-IV lacking DNA-binding domains (18.7 kDa), but not wildtype POU-IV (35.2 kDa) (Figure 3D), validating the specificity of the antibody.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3D

claim: 100% of the F2 pou-iv +/+ wildtype animals contracted at least one tentacle in response to touch.
source: In this study, a hair held in a tungsten needle holder was quickly depressed on the distal portion of each tentacle, and the presence/absence of the touch-response behavior of tentacles was scored for each animal; 100% of the F2 pou-iv +/+ wildtype animals that were examined (n = 44) contracted at least one tentacle in response to touch (Figure 4A and B; Figure 4—video 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4

claim: Only 35% of the F2 pou-iv -/- knockout animals showed any sign of tentacular retraction in response to touch.
source: In contrast, we observed that only 35% of the F2 pou-iv -/- knockout animals (n = 40) showed any sign of tentacular retraction in response to touch; 65% of the knockout mutants exhibited no discernable tentacular response to tactile stimuli (Figure 4C and D; Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4

claim: 65% of F2 pou-iv -/- knockout animals exhibited no discernable tentacular response to tactile stimuli.
source: In contrast, we observed that only 35% of the F2 pou-iv -/- knockout animals (n = 40) showed any sign of tentacular retraction in response to touch; 65% of the knockout mutants exhibited no discernable tentacular response to tactile stimuli (Figure 4C and D; Figure 4—video 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4

claim: 87% of F2 pou-iv +/- heterozygotes showed touch-induced tentacular responses.
source: The majority of F2 pou-iv +/- heterozygotes (87%, n = 62) showed touch-induced, tentacular responses; 13% did not show touch responses, suggestive of dose-dependent effects of POU-IV expression on the mechanosensory behavior.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data

claim: 13% of F2 pou-iv +/- heterozygotes did not show touch responses.
source: The majority of F2 pou-iv +/- heterozygotes (87%, n = 62) showed touch-induced, tentacular responses; 13% did not show touch responses, suggestive of dose-dependent effects of POU-IV expression on the mechanosensory behavior.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data

claim: The reduced tentacular response to touch in pou-iv -/- mutants is not due to the inability of tentacular muscles to contract.
source: The reduced tentacular response to touch in pou-iv -/- mutants is not due to the inability of tentacular muscles to contract, as pou-iv -/- mutants responded to crushed brine shrimp extract by contracting tentacles (100%, n = 8 animals; Figure 4—figure supplement 1; Figure 4—videos 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: pou-iv is specifically required for the touch-sensitive behavior of oral tentacles in N. vectensis.
source: Hence, pou-iv is specifically required for the touch-sensitive behavior of oral tentacles in N. vectensis, consistent with POU-IV having a role in regulating the development of the mechanosensory hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the behavioral data showing touch insensitivity in pou-iv mutants but normal muscle function

claim: The longitudinal muscles in the tentacle of F2 pou-iv -/- mutants developed normally.
source: At the primary polyp stage, F-actin labeling by phalloidin showed that the longitudinal muscles in the tentacle of F2 pou-iv -/- mutants developed normally (Figure 5A, D and G), consistent with the behavioral evidence demonstrating the ability of the mutant tentacles to contract in response to the brine shrimp extract.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Mature cnidocytes with cnidae fail to develop in pou-iv knockout mutants.
source: We have confirmed the previous finding that mature cnidocytes with cnidae fail to develop in pou-iv knockout mutants (Figure 5C,F,I; Tournière et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5, confirming a previous report

claim: Mature hair cells with stereovillar rootlets were lacking in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps.
source: In addition, we found that mature hair cells with stereovillar rootlets were lacking in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps (n = 6 animals), while mature hair cells formed normally in tentacles of pou-iv +/- (n = 6 animals) and pou-iv +/+ (n = 3 animals) siblings (Figure 5A–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Mature hair cells formed normally in tentacles of pou-iv +/- and pou-iv +/+ siblings.
source: In addition, we found that mature hair cells with stereovillar rootlets were lacking in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps (n = 6 animals), while mature hair cells formed normally in tentacles of pou-iv +/- (n = 6 animals) and pou-iv +/+ (n = 3 animals) siblings (Figure 5A–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Ciliary cone-like structures lacking stereovillar rootlets occurred in pou-iv -/- mutants.
source: Ciliary cone-like structures lacking stereovillar rootlets occurred in pou-iv -/- mutants (Figure 5G–I), raising the possibility that hair cells might undergo partial differentiation in pou-iv -/- mutants.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Stereovillar rootlets and cnidae were absent in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps.
source: Electron microscopic observations confirmed these findings. Stereovillar rootlets and cnidae were absent in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps (n = 2 animals) but were present in the tentacles of their wildtype siblings (n = 2 animals) (Figure 5J–L; Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Stereovillar rootlets and cnidae were present in the tentacles of wildtype siblings of pou-iv -/- polyps.
source: Electron microscopic observations confirmed these findings. Stereovillar rootlets and cnidae were absent in the tentacles of F2 pou-iv -/- polyps (n = 2 animals) but were present in the tentacles of their wildtype siblings (n = 2 animals) (Figure 5J–L; Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: A hair-cell-like cell in pou-iv -/- mutants has an apical ciliary cone without stereovillar rootlets, surrounded by support cells with characteristic electron-dense vacuoles.
source: We also confirmed by electron microscopy the presence of a hair-cell-like cell that has an apical ciliary cone without stereovillar rootlets, surrounded by support cells with characteristic electron-dense vacuoles that contribute microvilli to the ciliary cone in pou-iv -/- mutants (Figure 5K and L)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5

claim: Ciliary rootlets were observed in hair-cell-like cells in pou-iv -/- mutants.
source: ciliary rootlets were observed in these hair-cell-like cells in pou-iv -/- mutants (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3

claim: The lack of cnidae is consistent with the inability of pou-iv null mutants to capture prey.
source: The lack of cnidae is consistent with the inability of pou-iv null mutants to capture prey as previously reported (Tournière et al., 2020), but cannot explain the lack of tentacular contraction in response to touch.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of cnidae absence and a previous report

claim: Stereovillar rootlets provide stereovilli with structural resilience against physical damage and are necessary for normal mechanosensitivity in vertebrate hair cells.
source: Stereovillar rootlets provide stereovilli with structural resilience against physical damage and are necessary for normal mechanosensitivity in vertebrate hair cells (Kitajiri et al., 2010).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: Touch insensitivity of oral tentacles in pou-iv null mutants results, at least in part, from the failure of hair cells to generate structurally robust apical mechanosensory apparatus.
source: We therefore suggest that touch insensitivity of oral tentacles in pou-iv null mutants results, at least in part, from the failure of hair cells to generate structurally robust apical mechanosensory apparatus (see Discussion).
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation of missing stereovillar rootlets and knowledge about their function

claim: POU-IV(-) is distributed throughout the cytoplasm of POU-IV(-)-expressing cells in pou-iv -/- mutants.
source: A number of epithelial cells in the tentacular ectoderm were found to express POU-IV(-) (Figure 6A–C). In contrast to the primarily nuclear localization of POU-IV in wildtype animals (Figure 2), however, POU-IV(-) is distributed throughout the cytoplasm of POU-IV(-)-expressing cells in pou-iv -/- mutants (Figure 6A–F), presumably due to the lack of nuclear localization signal (located at the N-terminal end of the homeodomain; Sock et al., 1996) in POU-IV(-) (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6

claim: The epithelial cells bearing apical ciliary cones in pou-iv -/- mutants expressed POU-IV(-).
source: We found that the epithelial cells bearing apical ciliary cones in pou-iv -/- mutants expressed POU-IV(-) (Figure 6D–F) and therefore could represent partially differentiated hair cells that failed to undergo maturation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6

claim: Ncol3-positive immature cnidocytes in pou-iv -/- mutants expressed POU-IV(-).
source: By using immunostaining with an anti-Ncol3, we confirmed that Ncol3-positive immature cnidocytes in pou-iv -/- mutants indeed expressed POU-IV(-) (Figure 6G–I).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6

claim: None of the Ncol3-positive immature cnidocytes in pou-iv -/- mutants had distinct apical ciliary cones.
source: However, none of the Ncol3-positive immature cnidocytes in pou-iv -/- mutants had distinct apical ciliary cones (e.g. Figure 6J–L), suggesting that ciliary cone-bearing epithelial cells in pou-iv -/- mutants represent immature hair cells, and not immature nematocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6

claim: Hair cells appear to be present in their immature, yet morphologically differentiated, form in pou-iv -/- mutants.
source: Thus, hair cells appear to be present in their immature, yet morphologically differentiated, form in pou-iv -/- mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation of ciliary cone-bearing cells that are not cnidocytes

claim: The presence of partially differentiated hair cells in pou-iv -/- mutants supports the hypothesis that POU-IV regulates maturation, but not initial differentiation, of hair cells in N. vectensis.
source: The presence of partially differentiated hair cells in pou-iv -/- mutants supports the hypothesis that POU-IV regulates maturation, but not initial differentiation, of hair cells in N. vectensis.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation of immature hair cells in pou-iv mutants

claim: Kaede-positive immature hair cells in presumptive pou-iv -/- mutants developed morphologically normal basal neurites.
source: In these presumptive mutants, Kaede-positive immature hair cells were readily identifiable based on morphology and position; their cell bodies were pear-shaped and located in the superficial stratum of the tentacular ectoderm, some of which contained apical microvilli that are organized into a ciliary cone-like microvillar structure (Figure 6M and N). These immature hair cells, however, developed morphologically normal basal neurites (Figure 6O), indicating that pou-iv is not necessary for neurite extension in hair cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6

claim: pou-iv is not necessary for neurite extension in hair cells.
source: These immature hair cells, however, developed morphologically normal basal neurites (Figure 6O), indicating that pou-iv is not necessary for neurite extension in hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of normal neurites in immature hair cells of pou-iv mutants

claim: pou-iv is not required for the development of basal neurite-like processes in cnidocytes.
source: Neither is pou-iv required for the development of basal neurite-like processes in cnidocytes; basal processes were observed in Ncol3-positive immature cnidocytes (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2

claim: None of the POU-IV(-)-expressing epithelial cells examined in the tentacular ectoderm had TUNEL-positive, pyknotic nuclei indicative of apoptotic DNA fragmentation.
source: We have therefore tested whether pou-iv regulates hair cell survival in N. vectensis, by carrying out the terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end-labeling (TUNEL) assay in pou-iv -/- mutants. We found that none of the POU-IV(-)-expressing epithelial cells examined in the tentacular ectoderm (n = 100 cells across five primary polyps) had TUNEL-positive, pyknotic nuclei indicative of apoptotic DNA fragmentation, although TUNEL-positive nuclear fragments were commonly observed in the endoderm (Figure 6P–R).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 6

claim: In sea anemones, POU-IV does not appear to be directly involved in the survival of hair cells.
source: Thus, in sea anemones, POU-IV does not appear to be directly involved in the survival of hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TUNEL assay data showing no apoptosis in POU-IV-expressing cells

claim: 12,972 genomic sites were enriched in ChIP DNA.
source: We sequenced anti-POU-IV immunoprecipitated DNA and input DNA, and mapped the reads to the N. vectensis genome (Putnam et al., 2007). We identified 12,972 genomic sites that were enriched in ChIP DNA (i.e. ChIP peaks) (Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: Three motifs were enriched toward the center of ChIP peaks: rwrwaatmatgcattattaatatt (motif 1), rmataaataatgcattatttatky (motif 2), and tkcataaataatttatgmm (motif 3).
source: We then performed a de novo motif search and motif enrichment analysis, and found three motifs rwrwaatmatgcattattaatatt (motif 1; E = 5.2e-075), rmataaataatgcattatttatky (motif 2; E = 1.2e-052), and tkcataaataatttatgmm (motif 3; E = 4.8e-36) that were enriched toward the center of ChIP peaks (p = 3.5e-368 and p = 1.0e-138, respectively) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 7

claim: The three motifs showed significant sequence similarity to Homo sapiens POU4F1-, POU4F2-, and POU4F3-binding motifs.
source: When we compared these three motifs against the Jaspar database (Fornes et al., 2020), we discovered that they showed significant sequence similarity to Homo sapiens POU4F1-, POU4F2-, and POU4F3-binding motifs (Figure 7B; p < 10–5, p < 10–3, and p < 10–3, respectively), indicative of deep conservation of POU-IV-binding motifs across Cnidaria and Bilateria.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on motif comparison analysis shown in Figure 7

claim: The motifs identified contain the sequence AT(A/T)ATT(A/T)AT, which is nearly identical to the core recognition sequence of bilaterian POU-IV, AT(A/T)A(T/A)T(A/T)AT.
source: Indeed, the motifs we have identified contain the sequence AT(A/T)ATT(A/T)AT (shown in bold in motif sequences above), which is nearly identical to the core recognition sequence of bilaterian POU-IV, AT(A/T)A(T/A)T(A/T)AT (Gruber et al., 1997).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of the identified motifs with known bilaterian POU-IV-binding sequences

claim: The preference of GC residues 5' to the core recognition sequence is evident in motifs 1 and 2, and in bilaterian POU-IV-binding sequences, and therefore appears to be conserved.
source: In addition, the preference of GC residues 5' to the core recognition sequence is evident in motifs 1 and 2 (underlined in motif sequences above), and in bilaterian POU-IV-binding sequences (Gruber et al., 1997), and therefore appears to be conserved.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of the identified motifs with known bilaterian POU-IV-binding sequences

claim: The core recognition motif-like sequences are essential for DNA recognition by POU-IV.
source: We tested the ability of POU-IV to bind to the core recognition motif-like sequences by electrophoretic mobility shift assays (EMSAs), and confirmed that they were indeed essential for DNA recognition by POU-IV (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 7C

claim: In the last common ancestor of Cnidaria and Bilateria, POU-IV bound to the consensus DNA element GCAT(A/T)ATT(A/T)AT to regulate gene expression.
source: We infer that in the last common ancestor of Cnidaria and Bilateria, POU-IV bound to the consensus DNA element GCAT(A/T)ATT(A/T)AT to regulate gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the conservation of POU-IV-binding motifs across Cnidaria and Bilateria

claim: A total of 4188 candidate POU-IV downstream target genes were identified.
source: We next sought to identify downstream target genes of POU-IV, based on the criteria that a target gene has at least one POU-IV ChIP peak within the gene locus which includes the promoter region – 350 bp upstream and 100 bp downstream of the transcription start site – and the gene body. Using this criterion, we found a total of 4188 candidate POU-IV downstream target genes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: 577 genes were downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings.
source: We then examined which of these candidate POU-IV target genes were activated/repressed by POU-IV, using publicly available transcriptome data from NvPOU4 mutant polyps and their siblings (Tournière et al., 2020). Re-analysis of the transcriptome data identified 577 genes that were downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on re-analysis of published RNA-seq data

claim: 657 genes were upregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings.
source: and 657 genes that were upregulated in the mutants (Supplementary file 3) (adjusted p-value < 0.01).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on re-analysis of published RNA-seq data

claim: GO terms overrepresented in genes downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants included those related to nervous system function such as 'synaptic transmission' and 'detection of stimulus'.
source: Consistent with the previous report (Tournière et al., 2020), Gene Ontology (GO) terms overrepresented in genes downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants included those related to nervous system function such as 'synaptic transmission' and 'detection of stimulus' (Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on GO analysis of RNA-seq data, consistent with a previous report

claim: Out of the 577 genes downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings, 293 were POU-IV target genes.
source: Out of the 577 genes downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings, 293 were POU-IV target genes (Supplementary file 6)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: Out of the 657 genes upregulated in NvPOU4 mutants, 178 were POU-IV target genes.
source: while out of the 657 genes upregulated in NvPOU4 mutants (Supplementary file 7), 178 were POU-IV target genes
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: Among the POU-IV-repressed genes is the pou-iv gene itself.
source: Among the POU-IV-repressed genes is the pou-iv gene itself, indicating that POU-IV negatively regulates its own expression.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: POU-IV negatively regulates its own expression.
source: Among the POU-IV-repressed genes is the pou-iv gene itself, indicating that POU-IV negatively regulates its own expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the finding that pou-iv is among POU-IV-repressed genes

claim: 84 GO terms were overrepresented in the 293 genes directly activated by POU-IV, including terms related to nervous system function such as 'synaptic transmission'.
source: GO analysis found that 84 GO terms were overrepresented in the 293 genes directly activated by POU-IV, which include terms related to nervous system function such as 'synaptic transmission' (p-adjusted <0.05) (Supplementary file 8).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on GO analysis of integrated ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: No GO terms were significantly overrepresented in the 178 genes directly repressed by POU-IV.
source: No GO terms were significantly overrepresented in the 178 genes directly repressed by POU-IV (p-adjusted <0.05).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on GO analysis of integrated ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: A polycystin 1 (PKD1)-like gene is among the 577 genes significantly downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings.
source: To shed light on the mechanism by which POU-IV regulates hair cell maturation, we assessed which genes were directly activated by POU-IV in hair cells. Among the 577 genes significantly downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings is a transmembrane receptor-encoding polycystin 1 (PKD1)-like gene (JGI ID: 135278).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on RNA-seq data analysis

claim: The polycystin 1-like gene is specifically expressed in tentacular epithelial cells whose cell bodies are located in the superficial stratum of the pseudostratified epithelium, resembling the hair cell.
source: By using in situ hybridization, we found that this gene was specifically expressed in tentacular epithelial cells whose cell bodies were located in the superficial stratum of the pseudostratified epithelium, resembling the hair cell (Figure 8A–F).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 8

claim: The polycystin 1-like gene and another polycystin 1-like gene upstream together constitute a single polycystin 1-like gene.
source: We discovered by RTPCR that this gene and another polycystin 1-like gene (JGI ID: 218539) upstream – which was also one of the 577 genes significantly downregulated in NvPOU4 mutants relative to their siblings – together constitute a single polycystin 1-like gene.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on RTPCR data

claim: The transcript of the polycystin 1-like is 11,279 bases long and encodes a protein that is 3457 amino acids long.
source: The transcript of the polycystin 1-like is 11,279 bases long and encodes a protein that is 3457 amino acids long (Figure 8—figure supplement 1; GenBank accession number, OK338071).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on cDNA sequencing

claim: There are two POU-IV-binding motifs around the transcription start site of the polycystin 1 locus.
source: ChIP-seq data show that there are two POU-IV-binding motifs around the transcription start site of this locus (Figure 8G), suggesting that the polycystin 1-like gene is directly regulated by POU-IV.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8G

claim: The polycystin 1-like gene is directly regulated by POU-IV.
source: ChIP-seq data show that there are two POU-IV-binding motifs around the transcription start site of this locus (Figure 8G), suggesting that the polycystin 1-like gene is directly regulated by POU-IV.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the presence of POU-IV-binding motifs near the transcription start site

claim: The N. vectensis Polycystin 1-like protein was predicted to have a Polycystin 1-like domain structure, containing the extracellular PKD domain and REJ module that are uniquely shared by Polycystin 1 proteins.
source: The N. vectensis Polycystin 1-like protein was predicted to have a Polycystin 1-like domain structure, containing the extracellular PKD (polycystic kidney disease) domain and REJ (receptor for egg jelly) module that are uniquely shared by Polycystin 1 proteins (Moy et al., 1996; Bycroft et al., 1999)
evidence: This is a conclusion based on sequence analysis and comparison with known Polycystin 1 proteins

claim: Phylogenetic analysis robustly placed the newly discovered N. vectensis polycystin-1-like within the Polycystin 1 group.
source: We therefore generated an amino acid sequence alignment of the TOP domain and transmembrane domains of Polycystin 1 and Polycystin 2 proteins, and used it to carry out maximum likelihood phylogeny estimation. The results robustly placed the newly discovered N. vectensis polycystin-1-like within the Polycystin 1 group (Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by phylogenetic analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2

claim: The polycystin 1 reporter construct drove expression specifically in hair cells at the primary polyp stage.
source: To better resolve the cell type in which polycystin 1 is expressed, we generated a reporter construct using 3704 bp sequence encompassing the two POU-IV-binding motifs and upstream promoter region of the gene (scaffold 353:49,338–53,412). We injected this construct into wildtype zygotes and confirmed reporter gene expression specifically in hair cells at the primary polyp stage (Figure 8H–K).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by transgenic reporter data shown in Figure 8

claim: polycystin 1 expression is lost in pou-iv -/- mutants but not in their siblings.
source: In addition, we have validated by in situ hybridization that polycystin 1 expression is lost in pou-iv -/- mutants (n = 5) but not in their siblings (n = 3) (Figure 8L-S).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 8

claim: polycystin 1 is directly activated by POU-IV in hair cells.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that polycystin 1 is directly activated by POU-IV in hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence including ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, in situ hybridization, and reporter assays

claim: polycystin 1 represents the first molecular marker specific to cnidarian hair cells.
source: To our knowledge, polycystin 1 represents the first molecular marker specific to cnidarian hair cells.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding

claim: The adult metacell c79 represents the hair cell.
source: Both polycystin-like gene models (JGI IDs: 135278 and 218539) that are part of the newly discovered polycystin 1 are uniquely represented in one of Sebe-Pedros et al.'s transcriptomically defined adult cell types ('c79') referred to as the metacells (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018). We have therefore deduced that the adult metacell c79 represents the hair cell
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the unique expression of polycystin 1 in metacell c79

claim: Out of the 293 genes directly activated by POU-IV, 32 genes were represented in the adult metacell c79 (the presumptive hair cell).
source: Out of the 293 genes directly activated by POU-IV, we found a total of 32 genes that were represented in the adult metacell c79 (the presumptive hair cell) (Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: Three of the 32 genes activated by POU-IV in hair cells are not found in any other metacell: coagulation factor/neuropilin-like, CD59 glycoprotein-like, and polycystin 1.
source: Three of the 32 genes – coagulation factor/neuropilin-like (JGI gene ID: 202575), CD59 glycoprotein-like (NVE ID: 735; no JGI ID), and polycystin 1 – are not found in any other metacell.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on analysis of single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: No transcription factor-encoding genes were found to be activated by POU-IV in hair cells.
source: No transcription factor-encoding genes were found to be activated by POU-IV in hair cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on analysis of integrated ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: Five GO terms were overrepresented in POU-IV-activated genes in hair cells, including 'potassium ion transmembrane transport' and 'sensory perception of sound'.
source: GO analysis found that five GO terms were overrepresented in POU-IV-activated genes in hair cells (p-adjusted <0.05), including 'potassium ion transmembrane transport' and 'sensory perception of sound' (Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on GO analysis of integrated data

claim: Out of the 178 genes that are repressed by POU-IV, only two genes are represented in the adult metacell c79: pou-iv itself and peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase-like.
source: In contrast, out of the 178 genes that are repressed by POU-IV, only two genes – pou-iv itself and peptidylglycine alpha-amidating monooxygenase-like (JGI gene ID: 172604) – are represented in the adult metacell c79 (Supplementary file 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: POU-IV controls the maturation of hair cells by activating a cell-type-specific combination of effector genes that confer hair cell identity.
source: These results are consistent with the hypothesis that POU-IV controls the maturation of hair cells by activating a cell-type-specific combination of effector genes that confer hair cell identity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding that POU-IV activates a unique set of effector genes in hair cells

claim: Of the 293 genes activated by POU-IV, three genes were found in the cnidocyte metacell c8: two transmembrane propyl 4-hydroxylase-like genes and a serine transporter-like gene.
source: Of the 293 genes activated by POU-IV, we found three genes in c8, which consisted of two transmembrane propyl 4-hydroxylase-like genes (JGI gene IDs: 239358 and 118978) and a serine transporter-like gene (JGI gene ID: 238501) (Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: serine transporter-like and one of the hydroxylase-like genes are represented specifically in cnidocyte metacells and not in others.
source: serine transporter-like and one of the hydroxylase-like genes (JGI gene ID: 239358) are represented specifically in cnidocyte metacells and not in others (Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: Transcription factor-encoding genes were not found to be activated by POU-IV in cnidocytes.
source: As in hair cells, transcription factor-encoding genes were not found to be activated by POU-IV in cnidocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on analysis of integrated ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: Of the 178 genes that are repressed by POU-IV, 13 genes were found in the cnidocyte metacell c8, which included genes encoding zinc finger and Sox transcription factors.
source: Of the 178 genes that are repressed by POU-IV, 13 genes were found in the cnidocyte metacell c8, which included genes encoding zinc finger and Sox transcription factors (Supplementary file 11)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: There is no overlap in genes activated by POU-IV between hair cells and cnidocytes.
source: Importantly, we found no overlap in genes activated by POU-IV between hair cells and cnidocytes, which indicates that POU-IV controls the maturation of hair cells and cnidocytes by turning on the expression of distinct sets of genes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on integration of ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: POU-IV controls the maturation of hair cells and cnidocytes by turning on the expression of distinct sets of genes.
source: Importantly, we found no overlap in genes activated by POU-IV between hair cells and cnidocytes, which indicates that POU-IV controls the maturation of hair cells and cnidocytes by turning on the expression of distinct sets of genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding of no overlap in POU-IV-activated genes between hair cells and cnidocytes

claim: POU-IV may have a more significant role as a leaky repressor in cnidocytes than in hair cells.
source: In addition, POU-IV may have a more significant role as a leaky repressor – to fine-tune gene expression levels – in cnidocytes than in hair cells, as the proportion of POU-IV-repressed genes relative to the total number of POU-IV targets represented in a given metacell was substantially higher in the cnidocyte (13/16; 81.25%) than in the hair cell (3/35; 8.6%).
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the comparison of the proportion of POU-IV-repressed genes in hair cells versus cnidocytes

claim: The gene regulatory mechanisms by which POU-IV orchestrates the differentiation of hair cells and cnidocytes appear to be remarkably distinct.
source: Thus, the gene regulatory mechanisms by which POU-IV orchestrates the differentiation of hair cells and cnidocytes appear to be remarkably distinct.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding that POU-IV activates different genes and has different repression patterns in hair cells versus cnidocytes

claim: POU-IV plays a necessary role in regulating the maturation of mechanosensory hair cells in the sea anemone by directly activating the expression of cell-type-specific effector genes.
source: The results suggest that POU-IV plays a necessary role in regulating the maturation of mechanosensory hair cells in the sea anemone by directly activating the expression of cell-type-specific effector genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence from the study

claim: POU-IV is the terminal selector of hair cell identity in the sea anemone.
source: Our findings strongly support POU-IV being the terminal selector of hair cell identity in the sea anemone.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the evidence that POU-IV directly activates effector genes in postmitotic hair cells

claim: POU-IV is specifically involved in the maturation, and not progenitor proliferation, initial differentiation, or survival, of hair cells in the tentacular ectoderm in N. vectensis.
source: Several lines of evidence indicate that POU-IV is specifically involved in the maturation, and not progenitor proliferation, initial differentiation, or survival, of hair cells in the tentacular ectoderm in N. vectensis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple lines of evidence from the study

claim: POU-IV is unlikely to have roles in proliferation or generation of hair cell progenitor cells because it is postmitotically expressed in hair cells.
source: First, POU-IV is postmitotically expressed in hair cells in tentacular ectoderm, and thus is unlikely to have roles in proliferation or generation of their progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the postmitotic expression pattern of POU-IV

claim: The existence of differentiated hair cells in POU-IV null mutants implies that POU-IV is not involved in the initial differentiation of hair cells.
source: The existence of differentiated hair cells in POU-IV null mutants implies that POU-IV is not involved in the initial differentiation of hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation of immature hair cells in pou-iv mutants

claim: POU-IV is essential for maturation of hair cells.
source: However, the hair-cell-like cells of POU-IV null mutants failed to form a mature apical mechanosensory apparatus with stereovillar rootlets, indicating that POU-IV is essential for maturation of hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that hair cells in pou-iv mutants lack stereovillar rootlets

claim: POU-IV does not seem to be required for the survival of hair cells in the tentacles.
source: Lastly, we have found no evidence that the epithelial cells expressing the non-functional form of POU-IV protein in POU-IV null mutants undergo programmed cell death in the tentacular ectoderm. Thus, POU-IV does not seem to be required for the survival of hair cells in the tentacles.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the TUNEL assay data

claim: The loss of stereovillar rootlets in hair cells in pou-iv mutants suggests that the POU-IV transcription factor regulates the expression of genes that are involved in stereovillar development.
source: The loss of stereovillar rootlets in hair cells in pou-iv mutants suggests that the POU-IV transcription factor regulates the expression of genes that are involved in stereovillar development.
evidence: This is a conclusion inferred from the observation of missing stereovillar rootlets in pou-iv mutants

claim: Mouse PC-1 colocalizes with F-actin in inner ear hair cell stereovilli and is necessary for maintenance of stereovillar structure and normal hearing.
source: Interestingly, its mouse homolog (PC-1) colocalizes with F-actin in inner ear hair cell stereovilli and is necessary for maintenance of stereovillar structure and normal hearing (Steigelman et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: PC-1 has been shown to regulate actin cytoskeleton reorganization in canine kidney epithelial cells.
source: In addition, PC-1 has been shown to regulate actin cytoskeleton reorganization in canine kidney epithelial cells (Boca et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: If the function of Polycystin 1 in modulating the organization of actin cytoskeleton is broadly conserved, N. vectensis Polycystin 1 might control the structural integrity of stereovilli in hair cells through its interaction with F-actin.
source: If the function of Polycystin 1 in modulating the organization of actin cytoskeleton is broadly conserved, N. vectensis Polycystin 1 might control the structural integrity of stereovilli in hair cells through its interaction with F-actin.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the conservation of Polycystin 1 function

claim: POU-IV may direct stereovillar development in cnidarian hair cells by activating polycystin 1.
source: POU-IV may therefore direct stereovillar development in cnidarian hair cells by activating polycystin 1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the finding that polycystin 1 is a POU-IV target gene and knowledge about Polycystin 1 function

claim: The lack of tentacular response to tactile stimuli in pou-iv mutants could be due to functional defects in mechanotransduction channels.
source: We note, however, that it could additionally be because of the functional defects in mechanotransduction channels.
evidence: This is an alternative hypothesis proposed by the authors

claim: POU-IV is known to directly activate the expression of the mechanotransduction channel-encoding gene, mec-4, that is necessary for touch-cell function in C. elegans.
source: POU-IV is known to directly activate the expression of the mechanotransduction channel-encoding gene, mec-4, that is necessary for touch-cell function in C. elegans (Duggan et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: In epithelial cells of vertebrate kidneys, Polycystin 1 interacts with the calcium ion channel Polycystin 2 to form a complex that functions as a fluid flow sensor.
source: In epithelial cells of vertebrate kidneys, Polycystin 1 interacts with the calcium ion channel Polycystin 2 to form a complex that functions as a fluid flow sensor with Polycystin 1 acting as a mechanosensitive cell surface receptor and Polycystin 2 as an ion-permeant pore (reviewed in Delmas, 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to a review article

claim: The N. vectensis genome encodes polycystin 2.
source: The N. vectensis genome encodes polycystin 2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), which is co-expressed with polycystin 1 in the adult metacell c79 (i.e. the hair cell) (Supplementary file 9; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on genome analysis and single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: polycystin 2 is co-expressed with polycystin 1 in the adult metacell c79 (i.e. the hair cell).
source: The N. vectensis genome encodes polycystin 2 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2), which is co-expressed with polycystin 1 in the adult metacell c79 (i.e. the hair cell) (Supplementary file 9; Sebé-Pedrós et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, based on single-cell RNA-seq data

claim: Hair cells of the sea anemone Haliplanella luciae have been reported to respond to N-acetylated sugars by elongating their stereovilli.
source: Indeed, hair cells of the sea anemone Haliplanella luciae have been reported to respond to N-acetylated sugars by elongating their stereovilli (Mire-Thibodeaux and Watson, 1994, Watson and Roberts, 1995), indicative of chemosensory function.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: The role for POU-IV in mechanoreceptor development is broadly conserved across Cnidaria and Bilateria.
source: Our results indicate that the role for POU-IV in mechanoreceptor development is broadly conserved across Cnidaria and Bilateria.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings of this study and established knowledge from bilaterian models

claim: POU-IV-dependent regulation of mechanosensory cell differentiation is pervasive across Cnidaria and Bilateria, and likely predates their divergence.
source: These comparative data show that POU-IV-dependent regulation of mechanosensory cell differentiation is pervasive across Cnidaria and Bilateria, and likely predates their divergence.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparative data from Cnidaria and Bilateria

claim: POU-IV has a broad role in the differentiation of multiple neural cell types across Cnidaria and Bilateria.
source: We note, however, that POU-IV has a broad role in the differentiation of multiple neural cell types across Cnidaria and Bilateria.
evidence: This is a statement based on established knowledge from multiple studies

claim: It seems plausible that POU-IV was ancestrally involved in the differentiation of multiple neural cell types in addition to mechanosensory cells.
source: Therefore, it seems plausible that POU-IV was ancestrally involved in the differentiation of multiple neural cell types in addition to mechanosensory cells.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the broad role of POU-IV in neural development

claim: POU-IV is required for normal development of stereovilli in hair cells in both sea anemones and mice.
source: Interestingly, POU-IV is required for normal development of stereovilli in hair cells in both sea anemones (this study) and mice (Xiang et al., 1998), raising the possibility that POU-IV controlled the formation of the apical sensory apparatus of mechanosensory cells in the last common ancestor of Cnidaria and Bilateria, potentially via regulation of polycyctin 1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the findings of this study and a previous study in mice

claim: POU-IV may have controlled the formation of the apical sensory apparatus of mechanosensory cells in the last common ancestor of Cnidaria and Bilateria, potentially via regulation of polycyctin 1.
source: Interestingly, POU-IV is required for normal development of stereovilli in hair cells in both sea anemones (this study) and mice (Xiang et al., 1998), raising the possibility that POU-IV controlled the formation of the apical sensory apparatus of mechanosensory cells in the last common ancestor of Cnidaria and Bilateria, potentially via regulation of polycyctin 1.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the conservation of POU-IV function in stereovillar development

claim: In Bilateria, members of the Atonal basic-loop-helix-loop-helix transcription factor family appear to have a conserved role in positive regulation of POU-IV expression.
source: In Bilateria, members of the Atonal basic-loop-helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factor family appear to have a conserved role in positive regulation of POU-IV expression (reviewed in Leyva-Díaz et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to a review article

claim: Vertebrate atonal genes act upstream of pou-iv genes to drive the differentiation of inner ear hair cells.
source: For instance, vertebrate atonal genes act upstream of pou-iv genes to drive the differentiation of inner ear hair cells (Ikeda et al., 2015; Masuda et al., 2011; Yu et al., 2021) and retinal ganglion cells (Liu et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: C. elegans atonal ortholog lin-32 controls the expression of the pou-iv ortholog unc-86 in touch sensory neurons.
source: Similarly, C. elegans atonal ortholog lin-32 controls the expression of the pou-iv ortholog unc-86 in touch sensory neurons (Baumeister et al., 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation

claim: Cnidarians lack unambiguous atonal orthologs.
source: Although cnidarians lack unambiguous atonal orthologs, they have divergent bHLH genes that belong to the Atonal superfamily, which consists of Atonal and related bHLH gene families including Neurogenin, and NeuroD (Gyoja et al., 2012; Simionato et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: Cnidarians have divergent bHLH genes that belong to the Atonal superfamily.
source: Although cnidarians lack unambiguous atonal orthologs, they have divergent bHLH genes that belong to the Atonal superfamily, which consists of Atonal and related bHLH gene families including Neurogenin, and NeuroD (Gyoja et al., 2012; Simionato et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations

claim: Cnidocytes, in addition to hair cells, have basal neurite-like processes.
source: Interestingly, we unexpectedly found that cnidocytes, in addition to hair cells, had basal neurite-like processes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I-L), which has never been reported in cnidarian literature to our knowledge.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1
